title: Clement writes to Corinth (c. 96)
hookLine: the bishop of Rome writes to calm a quarrelling church

cards: The letter opens with an apology for being late. The church at Rome has been hit by sudden troubles, one after another, and only now can it turn to the news from Corinth. The news is bad.
A few headstrong people there have pushed out leaders who had served the church well, and the community is split. Word of the fight has traveled far enough that outsiders are talking.
So Rome writes a long letter to a church across the sea, with one aim: peace.

teach.b: First, who's writing. The letter comes from the church of God staying at Rome, to the church of God staying at Corinth. It never signs a name.
An early tradition gives it to Clement, whom Catholics count among the early bishops of Rome after Peter. Second, how he argues: not with threats, but with stories.

Jealousy, he says, has done damage since Cain and Abel, and in their own generation it struck down the greatest pillars of the Church, Peter and Paul. Third, a clever move. Corinth had quarreled before.
Pick up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul, Clement says, and read it again. Paul had written to them about the same sickness: one says I belong to Paul, another to Apollos, another to Cephas.

You took sides then, Clement says, and that was less shameful, because at least you were choosing among apostles and a man they trusted. Now you've thrown out good leaders because of a few people. Fourth, the cure.
Who among you is noble, or tender-hearted, or full of love?

teach.h: IF IT'S BECAUSE OF ME, I'LL GO.
teach.b: Let that person say: if this split is because of me, I'll go away, wherever you like, and do what the people want, only let the flock of Christ be at peace.

teach.h: LET THE FLOCK BE AT PEACE.
teach.b: Peace, here, isn't winning. It's being willing to step aside. He sends trusted messengers with the letter, and asks them to come back soon with news of peace.

Catholics have long read the letter as an early sign of the Roman church caring for the others. Other readers see one sister church helping another. Both can see a church that loved peace enough to write.

how: Catholics honor Saint Clement of Rome as an early pope and, by tradition, a martyr, and his name is among the saints remembered in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

games.q: what does “clement writes to corinth” mean?
o: a ruling that removed Corinth's leaders by force
Rome's early letter asking a split church for peace
Paul's first letter, sent from prison in Rome

s: the letter is signed by Clement
it comes in the name of the church at Rome. tradition names Clement as its writer.
Clement points the Corinthians back to Paul's letter
Paul had already written to them about taking sides.
Clement says peace comes when the right side wins
he asks the noble-hearted to be willing to step aside for peace.

games.q: you're at the center of the quarrel in Corinth. a letter from Rome arrives, asking the noble-hearted to do something. what does it ask?
o: hold your ground until you win.
say: if this is because of me, I'll go.
start a new church across town.
games.why: Clement asks the noble-hearted to offer to leave, if that brings peace, so that the flock of Christ can be at peace.

practice: Think of a disagreement near you, in your family, your parish, your group chat, and version three sentences in your head the way Clement might.

Own something first, an apology or a fault; remind them of something good you share; then say what you're willing to give up. Don't send it; let it sit in you, and if you pray, ask peace for the people in it.

wordCard.voice: Clement writes to Corinth. A long letter from the church at Rome to a split church, asking for humility and peace. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: peace — the word Clement's letter keeps returning to.

carryVoice: Your line: peace in the church. A whole letter, sent across the sea for it. See you tomorrow.
